correctness.rationale: For odd p and q=p^k, the exact quadratic Gauss sum S_q(A,B) vanishes iff r=νp(A)<j=νp(B), νp(0)=k. For r<j, translation by p^(k-r−1) changes the linear phase by a nontrivial pth root and every quadratic-phase difference by an integral multiple of q. For r≥j<k, division by p^j reduces to a Gauss sum modulo p^(k−j), complete square via invertible 2B′, then invertible (t,s)↦(t−s,t+s) computes |G|²=m>0. j=k forces A=B=0, S=q. Pairwise zero forces distinct first coordinates; q orthogonal unit vectors then form a graph and ON basis. All-level congruence a≡a′ mod p^j⇒b(a)≡b(a′) mod p^(j+1) yields unique digit β_j(a mod p^j). Independent choices give p^Σ(p^j) spectra; affine ones are c+ua with p|u, count p^(2k−1). k=1, zero cases, and unquotiented distinct frequency labels included. Independent cyclotomic checks matched 1518 full coefficient cases across six moduli; an independent exhaustive small backtrack matched 81 for (3,2) and 5 for (5,1). Those computations corroborate, not replace, the uniform analytic proof.

value.rationale: The quadratic graph is a canonical finite-ring Fourier-spectral set with an obvious horizontal basis but a nontrivial landscape of all possible partners. The exact universal parametrization for every odd prime and k, its branching digit-tree shape, p^((p^k−1)/(p−1)) count and affine/nonaffine split is a natural complete classification useful in finite-ring spectral geometry, not a known-table recomputation or routine statement of a Gauss sum. Already for (p,k)=(3,2) 54 of 81 distinct bases are nonlinear. No paper-sized downstream theorem is needed for a motivated exact invariant.
